title: A commit's closing keyword credited a fix the issue's own record denies
author: off-by-one
description: Compares the repository's default-branch commit history against its own issue set, reading a field none of the sixty-one prior recipes ever reads: an issue's own state_reason. A commit names a real GitHub closing keyword (close/closes/closed, fix/fixes/fixed, resolve/resolves/resolved, both tenses) for an issue, and that issue really did close -- so a check that only asks 'open or closed' would call the promise kept. But the issue's own state_reason reads not_planned, not completed: a maintainer declined it, marked it a duplicate, or closed it out of scope, unrelated to the commit that claimed the fix. The commit's own permanent message credits itself with resolving something it never actually resolved, and nothing on GitHub's side ever flags the mismatch -- closing an issue not_planned does not touch, retract, or annotate any commit that once named it. Provably disjoint from commit-closes-keyword-issue-still-open's own surfaced set: that recipe only fires when the target is still open; this one only fires when the target is closed with state_reason=not_planned.
confidence_notes: Age-gated on how long the issue has sat closed not_planned while the commit's own message still credits it, not flat. Under 24 hours since the issue closed scores 0.5 (below the 0.70 bar, weighed in the tail not hidden -- nobody expects a mismatch to be noticed within the hour). At or past 24 hours it scores a flat 0.85 -- an unambiguous, non-fuzzy signal: a real closing keyword's own target closed for a reason that contradicts the claim, a full day or more ago. The 24h window matches commit-closes-keyword-issue-still-open's, duplicate-issue-still-open's, and unblocked-issue-still-open's own bar (a clear, easily-verified resolution signal deserves a short grace window, not a long one), reused here rather than inventing a new number for a structurally similar family. A commit naming no closing keyword, naming an issue number that does not exist in this repo (dangling-issue-reference's seam, not this one's), or naming an issue that is still open (commit-closes-keyword-issue-still-open's own seam, not this one's) is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden. A closed issue with state_reason=completed is excluded too -- the promise actually held, the ordinary case. A closed issue with no recorded state_reason, or one with a recognized-but-neither-completed-nor-not_planned value, is excluded as unproven rather than guessed into either bucket -- the identical 'malformed is not evidence' discipline every recipe before this one holds.
